narrative_purpose: Illustrates relative dating and superposition: a tall stack of rock layers where the lowest is oldest, with a thin datable ash band wedged between layers - showing how a planet's history is read as a page-stack of time before any atomic clock is used.
subject: A towering canyon wall of horizontally layered rock strata, dozens of distinct bands stacked one above another in slightly different muted hues, the lowest bands clearly the deepest. A single thin, paler band of fine volcanic ash runs across the middle, sandwiched between thicker darker layers. Faint cyan-teal bioluminescent traces glow along a few of the bedding planes, as if life seeped along the seams. A small dark figure at the canyon floor for scale.
scene: A deep eroded canyon on Pandora at dusk, the layered wall rising out of shadow, hazy depth receding along the gorge.
camera: Looking up the sheer layered wall from near the canyon floor, slight low angle so the stack towers and the oldest layers loom at the base.
light: Dim cool ambient twilight, a faint warm rim catching the top of the wall, soft teal glow along the bioluminescent bedding seams.
palette: Deep indigo shadow, muted stone greys and dim rust browns banding the wall, scarce teal-cyan glow along seams, one pale band standing out.
style: Painterly geological field-study plate, textured rock, strong sense of stacked depth.
detail_level: Crisp banding and texture on the near wall, the distinct pale ash band clearly legible; the gorge depth softening into haze.
composition: The layered wall filling most of the frame as strong horizontal bands, the pale ash band on a third line, the tiny scale figure low for human reference.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette; bioluminescent glow restrained and only along seams. Naturalistic rock, not a textbook cross-section diagram.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no infographic styling, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon style
